Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Effect clocks and telegraphs

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Use Effect for replayable status durations and stacks, and Telegraph for a wind-up that applies gameplay on a chosen tick. Effect stores a game-defined kind, stack count and remaining ticks in four value bytes. effect_stack refreshes an existing kind up to a supplied stack cap and keeps the longer duration; otherwise it uses the first empty slot. It returns the affected slot index so a game can attach frame-owned attribution alongside it. Invalid arguments or full storage reject without mutation. effects_tick clears expired slots, including a nonempty slot accidentally assigned zero remaining time.

Definitions, damage/pulse behavior, credit and reaction rules belong to the game. Stack counts deliberately do not imply multiplicative movement or damage rules. Scrapyard keeps four effects and four corresponding {seat, generation} credits on each body; expiry clears both, and a new occupant cannot inherit old DOT credit.

Telegraph owns the remaining and original wind-up durations. Start it with a duration, tick it once per simulation step, and apply the payload only when telegraph_tick returns true. Cancellation clears both fields. Presentation can use telegraph_fraction; a shortened wind-up therefore still starts at zero and finishes at one. Geometry, rooting policy and the landing effect remain the caller's.

Odin
if boss.tele.left > 0 {
    if p.telegraph_tick(&boss.tele) {pound(world, boss, ctx)}
    return
}
if in_range && cooldown_ready {p.telegraph_start(&boss.tele, 48)}

tests/replay_effects/run.sh compares nine 4,096-tick stack/expiry/telegraph traces against the original procedures compiled in isolation, with native boundary and WASM checks. Cached results allow the repository tests to run without the sibling Scrapyard checkout; REPLAY_REQUIRE_BASELINE=1 requires the live comparison.
